question: In response to the recognition of pathogen and after receiving help from the T lymphocyte, a macrophage:

options.opa: Increases the expression of MHC class II molecules.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Recognition of pathogen -> Activation of macrophage -> Increases the expression of MHC class II molecules -> 95% CHAIN: Recognition of pathogen -> Activation of macrophage -> Inactivates the NADPH oxidase complex -> 80% CHAIN: Recognition of pathogen -> Activation of macrophage -> Possible entry into anergy state -> 70% CHAIN: Recognition of pathogen -> Activation of macrophage -> Unclear involvement in activating the RAG1-RAG2 complex -> 95%
analysis: In response to the recognition of a pathogen and after receiving help from the T lymphocyte, a macrophage typically increases the expression of MHC class II molecules to present antigens to T cells for further immune response activation.
